key_insight: StateDRIFT tailors randomised Hamiltonian sampling to the initial state and target observable, reducing estimation bias and variance while retaining qDRIFT’s guarantees through a provable truncation bound.
engineering_relevance: Problem-aware sampling can reduce circuit depth and two-qubit gate requirements for estimating quantum dynamics at a target accuracy.
method: Optimise term-sampling probabilities at each depth to target bias and/or variance.
Use initial-state observables and commutators to inform the optimisation.
Estimate required quantities with classical surrogates, such as tensor networks, or classical shadows.
evidence_signal: Tests on short-time lattice and molecular dynamics up to 18 qubits included a BeH2 example reducing two-qubit gates from 11,201 to 983 at a given accuracy.
watch_item: Practical savings depend on the cost and accuracy of estimating the state-dependent quantities needed for sampling optimisation.
paper_title: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
